subject: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@finedge.ai>
Cc: procurement@finedge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:09:00 -0700
Subject: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise commercial proposal that aligns commit bands with the operational levers you care about: batching/caching credits and a quantization evaluation allowance. I attached a brief one-pager (FinEdge_Redwood_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf) with the numbers but called out the highlights below so we have something to iterate on quickly.

Proposal highlights (starter):
- 6-month commitment / prepaid credits model (flexible settlement):
  • Silver (base): $25k/month commit -> 250M token credits/month + 10% batching/caching credit
  • Gold: $75k/month commit -> 900M token credits/month + 18% batching/caching credit
  • Platinum: $150k/month commit -> 2.0B token credits/month + 25% batching/caching credit
- Quantization allowance: one free 30-day quantization evaluation per quarter (up to 3 test runs) plus guidance from our inference team; production use requires a modest quantization license add-on.
- Roll-forward for unused batching/caching credits within the commitment period (not beyond the period).
- Quality guardrail: if you see >7% delta in key generation quality metrics after quantization rollback/mitigation (we’ll define the metrics in the mutual action plan), Redwood will pause auto-quantized rollouts for your workload until mutually agreed fixes are applied.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which commit band you want to price (Silver/Gold/Platinum).
2) Agree a short mutual action plan for the quantization evaluation — we’ll assign an engineer for a 2-week POC.
3) Procurement: if those numbers look reasonable we can issue a formal SOW and DocuSign for the 6-month prepay.

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through.

—
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: FinEdge_Redwood_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf (1 page PDF)
From: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@finedge.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finedge.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances

Rafael —

Thanks for the clean breakdown. A few follow-ups from our side after we reviewed internally:

1) We liked the idea of batching/caching credits as a separate pool (that helps with bursty inference patterns). Two asks: can batching credits be used for both prefix caching and KV-cache warmup, and can unused batching credits be reallocated across months within the 6-month window?

2) On quantization: we will absolutely run the 30-day evaluation, but we need clarity on production limits — specifically: can we run up to 50% of traffic on a quantized variant for up to 30 days as a canary without extra license fees (beyond the evaluation)? We want to do staged canary traffic during rollout.

3) Commercial: if we sign a 6-month prepay today, would Redwood consider a small upward movement in the discount band (e.g., move Gold to 20% batching credit instead of 18%, or an additional 5% off list for the first month) to help justify the upfront payment to our CFO?

Procurement: looping in procurement to flag we’ll need SOC2 evidence and a standard SLA appendix.

Can we set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to work these items?

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Carter
Head of ML Platform | FinEdge
Sophie.Carter@finedge.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@finedge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karl <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@finedge.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances

Sophie —

Appreciate the concrete asks. Looping Marissa (commercial lead) and Karthik (Applied ML / inference optimization) to confirm the operational and commercial guardrails.

Quick answers from my side while they weigh in:
- Batching/caching credit scope: yes, they can be used for both prefix (response reuse) and KV cache warmup. We’ll call it a single batching credit pool that is honored by route; we can allow reallocation inside the 6-month commitment window but not beyond (we can show the ledger in the Console).
- Quantized canary: we can permit staged canaries up to 50% traffic for 30 days within the evaluation allowance, provided we have the agreed quality metrics and rollback criteria documented in the MAP. Karthik — can you confirm the recommended metric thresholds and what telemetry we’ll need from the FinEdge side?

Marissa / Karthik: Sophie’s procurement has flagged SOC2 and a standard SLA appendix + a small commercial concession request (Gold -> 20% batching credit OR additional 5% one-time first-month credit). What flexibility do we have on a 6-month prepay?

I’m available 10:00–11:30 PT tomorrow for a quick sync.

—
Rafael

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances

Hi Sophie / Rafael —

Thanks for the context. Confirming commercial flexibility and attaching an updated pricing deck (RDW-pricing-deck-v3.pdf) with two short alternative concessions we can offer for a 6-month prepay:

Option A (balance):
- Gold band moves to 20% batching/caching credit (from 18%).
- One-time onboarding credit = 5% off invoice for month 1.
- Batching credit pool is transferable between months within the 6-month window.
- Quantization: evaluation allowance as Rafael described; production quantization license discounted by 50% for the first 3 months of paid usage.

Option B (higher commit):
- 9-month commitment at Platinum-level economics for the first 6 months (effectively front-loading higher credits); we can discuss specifics if you want longer runway.

Operational / technical notes (Karthik):
- Karthik recommends the following metric thresholds for canary:
  • Generation quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/MDL-equivalent) < 5% for primary metric or rollback.
  • Latency increase < 15% p90.
  • Error rate difference < 1% absolute.
- Telemetry needed from FinEdge: sample prompt set (5–10k examples) and baseline metric exports for 14 days prior to canary. We’ll run quantized test variants in our Dedicated sandbox for the 30-day window.

Procurement / legal: we can provide SOC2 report and a standard SLA appendix; will surface DocuSign link once you confirm Option A vs B.

Next steps: Sophie — if Option A looks good I’ll pull a final SOW and send via DocuSign; Rafael — happy for you to schedule the 30-min call with Sophie and procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: RDW-pricing-deck-v3.pdf (6 slides)
From: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@finedge.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finedge.ai, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit bands, batching credits & quantization allowances

Marissa / Rafael —

Thanks — Option A looks like a clean path. Two remaining asks before we sign:
1) Please send the SOC2 summary and the SOW with the explicit definitions for the quantization MAP (we’ll need the metric names + rollback thresholds in the SOW).
2) Can you include the short one-page appendix that calls out how batching credits are consumed (order of operations: prefix cache first, then KV warmups, then live batch application) so our finance folks understand the ledger behavior?

If you can get those two things into DocuSign early tomorrow we’ll aim to finalize the SOW and get procurement to countersign by EOD Friday.

If you want to route the DocuSign to my direct email for fastest turnaround: sophie.carter@finedge.ai

Appreciate the quick cadence — excited to get this live.

Cheers,
Sophie
